evidence: Migration 0119_outreach_health_id.sql (placeholder; releases right after 0118) plus its runtime-grants.sql block. WHAT IT DOES: a volunteer or organiser at an outreach group (outreach.registration.write, a member of the registration's campaign, under the registration's own row-level security) creates a patient Health ID for a person they registered, from the registration's name, sex and phone only, after the person proves an email address with a 6-digit code (email only tonight). New owner-only tables identity.outreach_health_id_challenges (a keyed verifier of the code, never the code; the email's ciphertext and lookup HMAC; expiry; attempts) and identity.outreach_registration_health_ids (one per registration: patient, Health ID, who, when; immutable). The registration tables and 0115's rule G are unchanged (an outreach group still never links an existing Health ID). SECURITY DEFINER commands for the Identity runtime in the volunteer's delegated session refuse a registration not visible, redacted, under 18, without a phone, at a suspended, sealed (demo or QA) or non-outreach group; an email or phone already on a Health ID (never saying whose); more than 3 codes per registration in 24 hours or one within 60 seconds. Confirmation counts failed attempts (answering an outcome rather than raising), then creates the account (no password, pending_reset, email verified), the patient (no date of birth), its Health ID identifier, CONTACT_VERIFIED assurance and the registration's Health ID record, with one audit row (ids only). The Outreach runtime reads the Health IDs created for registrations it can see. The person sets a password later with Forgot password by email. Precondition: identity and outreach tables have one owner; patient and account tables do not force row-level security.
